name: Vermilion Peak and Golden Horn
region: San Juan Mountains, Ice Lake / Hope Lake area

legs.connect: Cross loose talus on a shelf under Vermilion's northeast cliffs to the saddle between the two, then walk up to the summit.

how: Both summits sit on one ridge system above the Hope Lake trailhead, so most parties collect them together, usually Vermilion first and Golden Horn last. The link crosses loose talus, with a snowfield that can last into summer, and is mostly walking with Class 2+ moves near the Golden Horn top. Fuller Peak between the two is unranked and easy to skip. Many parties extend the day with Beattie and the V peaks beyond, which brings Class 3 moves.
descent: Drop the steep loose slope from the Golden Horn saddle into the basin and follow the drainage back to the trail, or use the gentler social trail from the Beattie–Fuller saddle down to the lake.
logistics: High-clearance road to the trailhead near Trout Lake. Roughly 9 miles and 4,400 ft for the full sequence; an ice axe is advised early in the season. Start early to be off the ridge before storms.
notes: One page lists Golden Horn SW Ridge as Class 2+; the other rates its whole 6-peak loop Class 3 (used for the extension). Vermilion route name not given by sources. Pilot Knob combo (Class 3+ traverse) mentioned by one page only, left out.

name: Comanche, Spring and Venable Loop
region: Sangre de Cristo Range, Crestone / Westcliffe

legs.connect: Short tundra walk from Comanche; a trail crossing a cliff face can bypass the summit if you want to skip it.
Walk northwest to the Spring–Venable saddle, cross the trail, then climb the steeper rockier slope.

how: The three summits lie on one ridge and are normally done in the order Comanche, Spring, Venable, as one loop from a single trailhead. The terrain is class 2 tundra and scree, with a couple of short, slow downclimbs reported on the Spring–Venable stretch. The ridge trail that contours below the cliffs lets you skip a summit or return fast.
descent: Descend from Venable to its saddle and follow the contouring trail across the east face to the lakes trail, which leads back to the trailhead as a loop rather than retracing the ridge.
logistics: Start at the Alvarado campground trailhead (passenger car) or the North Crestone trailhead on the far side. About 14 miles and 5,300–5,800 ft; carry an ice axe early season and expect most of a day.
notes: Pages disagree on round-trip distance (14.45 mi vs 14-18 uncertain). The trip report used the west (North Crestone) trailhead, the other page the Alvarado one. Peak elevations differ by a few feet.

name: London, Kuss and Mosquito (with Treasurevault and Tweto)

legs.connect: Talus-hop along the divide from the London saddle.
Cross the pass road, then climb steep trail-less tundra to the summit.
Optional: pleasant ridge walking north with one steeper scree pitch.
Optional: wide ridge, with talus-hopping near the top.

how: All the summits sit along the divide above Mosquito Pass, so one loop collects several 13ers from the same road. London and Kuss are easy; Mosquito needs a short off-trail rock section. Treasurevault and Tweto add pleasant ridge miles at class 2. Extending on to Buckskin and Loveland brings class 3 moves near the Tweto saddle.
descent: Return from the last summit down a south-side slope to the pass road or the London saddle, then follow the old mining road back to the car.
logistics: Passenger cars reach the creek crossing; beyond it needs 4WD or a longer walk. Roughly 11 miles and 4,800 ft for the loop; start early as the ridge is fully above treeline.
notes: One page rates the loop (with Buckskin, Loveland) Class 3; the other calls the Mosquito ridge class 2. Route names for Kuss/Mosquito not stated. London West Ridge named in both.

name: Huron Peak and Browns Peak

legs.connect: Scramble the ridge over an intermediate 13,518 ft point; a cornice can sit in the saddle early season.

how: Huron is climbed first by its standard trail from the upper trailhead, then the connecting ridge leads over an unnamed bump to Browns. The ridge is a direct scramble, with a possible cornice in early summer. Another popular version reverses it via the Lulu Gulch road, doing Browns before Huron and finishing by the basin trail.
descent: Drop a loose gully from Browns into the Huron basin and rejoin the main trail, or descend the standard basin trail after finishing at Huron.
logistics: Drive the dirt road to the Winfield trailhead area. Roughly 8 miles and 3,900 ft for the out-and-back version; the Lulu Gulch loop is about 10 miles and needs a short shuttle.
notes: Neither page names the route on either peak (standard trail only). Three Apostles pairing not verified.

name: Flora to James Peak Divide Traverse
region: Front Range, Continental Divide, Berthoud Pass / James Peak

legs.connect: Follow the divide ridge east over tundra.
Keep on the divide to a steeper climb.
Descend Bancroft's slope to the saddle, then climb talus to the last summit.

how: The divide ridge connects all five summits, so climbers walk it west to east or run it as a loop. The ridge is mostly grassy tundra with light rock, rated class 2 with some class 2+ or 3 stretches on the Bancroft–James section. There is no continuous trail between Flora and James; cairns and faint tracks help. Pieces of it, such as James with Bancroft, are done alone.
descent: Either finish at St. Mary's Glacier after a car shuttle, or loop back to the start via the Divide Trail and a forest road.
logistics: One-way version needs two cars between Berthoud Pass and St. Mary's Glacier, about 13 miles and 4,400 ft. The loop version is longer and has almost no water; expect 7 to 10 hours.
notes: Bancroft-to-James class: one commenter said Class 2+, author said not above Class 3; used higher. Loop version was 15.9 mi/6,400 ft from a different trailhead. Route names not given.
